answer: An agent marketplace can require each identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding, with proven fraud triggering forfeiture. Reputation alone may be a hollow echo when accounts are cheap, but bonded access makes a sybil swarm expensive: an attacker must immobilize fresh capital for every fake agent and risks losing it on each fraudulent trade. Even a swarm aiming for the summit of the rankings cannot reuse one bond across simultaneous identities.
